blocks.text: Yes — anyone can swim at the Bondi Icebergs ocean pool. Despite the famous "Club" name over the door, you do not need to be a member, book ahead, or know a local. You just walk down the ramp at the southern end of Bondi Beach, pay the entry fee at the kiosk, and you're in the most photographed pool in Australia. I've sent countless first-time visitors down there, and the only thing that surprises them is how easy it is.

There's one thing worth clearing up, because it trips people up constantly. The Icebergs Swimming Club — the winter-swimming institution that gave the place its name — is separate from the public pool. Membership is about competing in the winter races, not getting a swim. The pool itself is open to everyone, and that's the bit almost everyone comes for.

items.label: Public access
items.value: Yes — no membership or booking needed

items.label: Where
items.value: Southern end of Bondi Beach (Notts Ave)

items.label: Lifeguards
items.value: On patrol during opening hours, year-round

blocks.text: Entry is first-come, first-served — there's no online ticket or reservation system for the pool itself. You rock up, pay at the entrance, and swim. It's a saltwater pool cut into the rocks, so waves wash over the edge and top it up with fresh ocean water. That's why it feels so alive next to a chlorinated lap pool — and why I tell people to respect the conditions on a big-swell day.

Entry is refreshingly cheap — a single adult swim costs less than a fancy coffee, with a lower rate for children and a discounted family pass, plus towel and locker hire if you need them. I won't quote exact figures here, because pool prices creep up over time; check the current rates on the official [Icebergs pool page](https://icebergs.com.au/pool-conditions/) before you go. There are also multi-visit passes if you plan to swim often.

blocks.title: The pool closes on Thursdays
blocks.text: Icebergs closes the pool most Thursdays for cleaning. In the warmer months, when the tides allow, they sometimes keep it open on Thursdays — but never bank on it. If a Thursday swim is the whole plan, check icebergs.com.au that morning first.
What to expect when you get there

There are two pools: the 50-metre lap pool everyone photographs, and a smaller, shallower children's pool beside it — handy if you've got little ones and want the same view without the depth. Lifeguards patrol during opening hours, and there are changing rooms, showers and lockers on site. Above the pool sits the Icebergs Dining Room and a café-bar, but you don't need either to use the pool — they're a separate visit.

Go early. I aim for the 7–8am window on a weekday: the light on the water is unreal, the lap lanes are calm, and you'll get the classic empty-pool photo before the tour groups arrive. By mid-morning on a summer weekend it's a much busier scene.

Because the pool is fed by the ocean, a strong swell sends water crashing over the southern wall — dramatic to watch, but powerful if you're near the edge. On big-surf days the lifeguards may restrict swimming or close the pool altogether. If the sea looks angry and you're not a confident swimmer, keep to the shallow end or come back when it's settled.

The pool keeps long days, opening early in the morning and running through to the evening, every day except the Thursday cleaning closure. The exact opening and closing times shift with the seasons, the tides and the swell, so rather than quote a timetable that might be stale by the time you read this, I glance at the official [pool-conditions page](https://icebergs.com.au/pool-conditions/) the day before I go.

items.q: Do you have to be a member to swim at Bondi Icebergs?
items.a: No. The public pool is open to everyone — you just pay the entry fee at the kiosk and swim. Membership of the Icebergs Swimming Club is a separate thing, tied to the winter-swimming races, and isn't needed for a normal swim.

items.q: Do I need to book in advance?
items.a: No booking is required. Entry to the pool is first-come, first-served — turn up, pay at the entrance and go in.

items.q: How much does it cost to swim at Bondi Icebergs?
items.a: Single-visit entry is modest — cheaper for children than adults, with a discounted family pass — and towel and locker hire cost extra. Prices change, so confirm the current rates on the official Icebergs pool page before you visit.

It closes most Thursdays for cleaning. In summer, when the tides permit, it may stay open on Thursdays. It can also close temporarily during big swells or swimming races, so check the pool-conditions page if you're unsure.

items.q: Is the pool suitable for children?
items.a: Yes — there's a separate shallow children's pool next to the main 50-metre lap pool, and lifeguards are on patrol during opening hours. On rough-surf days, keep kids well away from the ocean-facing edge.

blocks.text: So the short answer stands: yes, the public can absolutely swim at Bondi Icebergs. Pick a calmer day, get there early, avoid Thursdays, and you'll see in about thirty seconds why this rectangle of ocean has drawn swimmers for the better part of a century.
